memos.headline: Momentum leaders S07, S08, S10 near highs; S01 and S03 in clear downtrends — favor strength, fade weakness
memos.body: I see a sharp bifurcation in the universe today. S07 is printing a fresh 52-week high with RSI 80.9 and +17.7% over four weeks — parabolic but undeniably the strongest relative-strength name (+14.3% vs SPY over 4w). S08 and S10 sit within 1% of their highs with strong 12-week relative strength (+14.5% and +7.4% vs SPY respectively), though S08's RSI at 71 and +10.9% extension above the 50d mean warrant caution on new entries. On the weak side, S01 trades 15.3% off its high with RSI 39.1 and is 6.2% below its 200d mean — a textbook downtrend — while S03 is 9.3% off its high, below its 50d mean, and bleeding relative strength at -8.9% vs SPY over four weeks. S02's bear-market rally (+14.2% in 4w) is impressive but the stock remains 42.4% off its 52-week high and 10.3% below its 200d mean, making it a counter-trend bounce I'd rather watch than chase.

views.note: At 52w high with dominant relative strength (+14.3% vs SPY 4w, +15.0% 12w); RSI 80.9 is stretched so I'd trail a stop near 465 (roughly the 50d area) — a close below that level changes my view.
Within 0.4% of 52w high, +14.5% relative strength vs SPY over 12w, RSI 71 is elevated but not extreme; a break below 235 (approx 50d mean) would flip me neutral.
Near highs with +71.1% 26w return and solid relative strength, but ATR of 2.96% and +31.1% above 200d mean signal volatility risk; would reassess below 178.
Massive 12w return of +38.1% and +31.6% above 200d mean suggest overextension despite strong trend; waiting for a pullback toward the 50d area before adding.
Healthy uptrend (+15.5% above 200d) with moderate RSI 55 and low drawdown, but 12w relative strength vs SPY is only +0.6% — not compelling enough to chase.
Sharp 4w rally of +14.2% but still 42.4% off highs and below the 200d mean — this is a counter-trend bounce, not a new uptrend; need a close above 400 to turn constructive.
Flat to negative over 12w and 26w, -8.4% relative strength vs SPY over 12w, and 9.7% off highs — no trend to ride here.
Below both 50d and 200d means, RSI 39.1, -15.3% drawdown, and -10.9% relative strength vs SPY over 12w — clear downtrend; would reconsider only above 160.
Trading below 50d mean with RSI 41.6 and -8.9% relative strength vs SPY over 4w; needs to reclaim 227 (approx 50d) to neutralize the bearish setup.
Steady uptrend with low volatility (ATR 1.42%) and modest RSI 56.4, but 12w relative strength vs SPY is -3.8% — a market-performer at best right now.

memos.headline: S10 and S04 Lead on Earnings Power; S09 and S02 Show Cash-Flow Compression Risk
memos.body: I see the clearest durable earnings power in S10 and S04. S10 posted 56.5% net margins on $46.7B revenue with YoY revenue growth of +55.6% and net income growth of +59.2%, all on minimal debt of $8.5B — an extraordinary combination. S04 delivered 35.6% net margins, +18.1% revenue growth, and +23.6% net income growth on a clean $43.2B debt load. On the other end, S09 and S02 concern me: S09's revenue fell 12.4% YoY with net income down 23.4% on an 8.7% margin, while S02 grew revenue 12.9% but saw net income decline 19.2% to a razor-thin 3.1% margin against $79.2B in debt — classic cash-flow compression I refuse to pay for. I would need to see margin stabilization in S09 and S02 before reconsidering, specifically net margins recovering above 12% and 5% respectively.

views.note: 56.5% net margin, +55.6% YoY revenue growth, minimal $8.5B debt — best earnings quality in the universe by a wide margin.
35.6% net margin with +18.1% revenue growth and +23.6% net income growth on manageable $43.2B debt signals durable earnings power.
29.2% net margin, +13.8% revenue growth, +19.4% net income growth, and only $14.8B debt make this a high-quality compounder.
Revenue of $167.7B growing +13.3% with net income surging +34.7% YoY shows strong operating leverage, though 10.8% margin leaves less cushion.
Solid 24.9% margin and +9.6% revenue growth, but $91.8B debt load and decelerating income growth (+9.3%) temper enthusiasm.
17.3% margin and +15.3% net income growth are decent, but only +1.7% revenue growth and $30.4B debt suggest limited upside.
33.4% margin is attractive but revenue declined 10.5% YoY and $419.8B total debt is an outsized liability; need revenue stabilization.
Revenue flat at -0.7% YoY with net income down 18.7% and $31.7B debt on only $16.6B revenue signals margin erosion.
Revenue down 12.4% and net income down 23.4% with an 8.7% margin — clear cash-flow compression on $33.6B debt.
Despite +12.9% revenue growth, net income fell 19.2% to a 3.1% margin against $79.2B debt — earnings quality is deteriorating.

memos.headline: Fed in Cautious Easing Mode With Sticky Inflation—Favor Duration-Sensitive Growth Over Cyclicals
memos.body: I see the Fed firmly in an easing regime: the upper bound has dropped 75bp over the past year to 4.25%, with a 25bp cut in the last three months alone, while unemployment holds steady at 4.3% and CPI runs at 2.9% y/y—still above target but decelerating. The 10y yield has fallen 22bp over three months to 4.13%, and the 2s10s curve has re-steepened to +55bp from near-flat a year ago, consistent with a mid-cycle easing narrative rather than recession panic. I have moderate conviction that this gradual easing backdrop supports duration-sensitive growth and banks benefiting from a steeper curve, while I am cautious on pure cyclicals given the labor market is flat rather than accelerating. A September CPI print above 3.0% y/y or a surprise uptick in unemployment above 4.5% would force me to revisit this regime call.

views.note: Duration-sensitive growth benefits from falling 10y yields and continued Fed easing with 10y down 22bp in 3 months.
Banks gain from a steepening yield curve—2s10s spread widened 39bp y/y to +55bp, improving net interest margins.
Staples offer defensive positioning but limited upside in a gradual easing regime with no recession signal from labor data.
Cyclicals lack a catalyst with unemployment flat at 4.3% and no clear acceleration in growth; staying on the sidelines.
Energy faces headwinds from a slowing but not recessionary economy; easing policy historically rotates flows toward growth over commodities.
Rate-sensitive sectors benefit as the Fed eases further; the 75bp y/y decline in the upper bound supports valuation expansion.

memos.headline: Limited Sentiment Signal Across Universe; S07 New Debt Obligation and S02 Elevated Disclosure Activity Stand Out
memos.body: I see a quiet tape from a sentiment perspective—most filings are routine corporate housekeeping with no strong narrative shift detectable. S07 drew my attention with a material definitive agreement creating a direct financial obligation on 2025-09-03, which could weigh on tone if leverage concerns surface, though the earlier 'Other Events' filing on 2025-08-28 gave no price signal I can measure. S02 has been unusually active with three Reg FD disclosures (including an amendment) in a three-week span, suggesting management is proactively shaping the narrative—this volume of disclosure often precedes a tone inflection. S10's earnings-related 8-K on 2025-08-27 produced a muted -0.8% price reaction, implying the market had already priced in a soft result and sentiment may be bottoming. S04's director change filed 2025-09-30 is too fresh to have generated a durable tone shift, so I remain neutral there.

views.note: New material debt obligation may attract negative tone as leverage narrative builds; limited upside sentiment catalyst visible.
Elevated Reg FD disclosure cadence suggests management is front-running a narrative shift, which historically precedes improving tone.
Muted -0.8% reaction to earnings 8-K suggests bad news was priced; tone may be bottoming but no clear catalyst for reversal yet.
Director departure/appointment filed just days ago—too early for a durable sentiment read; watching for follow-through.
Two 'Other Events' filings in quick succession are ambiguous without detail; no directional tone signal.
Bylaw amendment is routine governance; unlikely to move sentiment needle.
Director change in mid-August is stale from a sentiment standpoint with no follow-on filings to sustain a narrative.

memos.headline: Policy Uncertainty Elevated but Easing; Falling Oil Prices Signal Demand-Side Geopolitical Risk
memos.body: I note that the Economic Policy Uncertainty Index sits at 438.91, down 10.1% over the past month but still up 16.7% over three months, suggesting that while the acute phase of policy shock may be fading, the structural overhang from trade and sanctions policy remains material. WTI crude at $61.28/bbl has dropped 10.7% over three months, which I read as a demand-side signal consistent with slowing global activity—possibly reflecting the cumulative drag of export controls and tariff escalation rather than a supply glut. VIX at 16.63 and HY OAS at 2.81% are both benign, indicating credit and equity vol markets are not yet pricing a hard geopolitical tail. I have moderate conviction that energy-exposed and China-supply-chain-dependent names face asymmetric downside if policy uncertainty re-accelerates, while domestically oriented names are relatively insulated. A reversal in the EPU trend or new sanctions/export-control announcements would change my view.

views.note: 8-K Other Events filing in late August provides no clear geopolitical catalyst; holding neutral pending further detail on any supply-chain or policy exposure.
Two 8-K Other Events filings in early September suggest corporate activity but without specifics I cannot assess geopolitical exposure; elevated EPU warrants caution.
Three Reg FD filings in Aug-Sep hint at active investor communication, possibly around policy-sensitive topics; the still-elevated EPU and falling oil prices keep me neutral until clarity emerges.
With WTI down 10.7% over three months and EPU still elevated at 439, energy-linked or export-dependent names face headwinds from both demand destruction and policy risk.
Benign VIX and tightening HY spreads favor domestically oriented names with limited geopolitical exposure; low confidence given sparse company-specific evidence.
Elevated 3-month EPU trend (+16.7%) and falling crude suggest caution on names with significant international or commodity-linked revenue streams.
